state.misconception_label: Believes f(x - a) translates the function up a units

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text:
I have: What transformation maps the graph of \(y=f(x) \) to the graph of \( y=f(x-3) \). I got Translation by vector
\(
\left[\begin{array}{l}
0 \\
3
\end{array}\right]
\) because I'm not sure I worked it out the right way.

turn_history.text: Um, well I saw the minus 3 in the brackets and I thought that meant we move down by 3, but then I got confused because that would be negative, so I just put it as moving up by 3 instead? I'm not really sure why the minus sign is there or what it actually means for the graph though.

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: Can you explain why you think moving up by 3 units is the correct transformation when the function is \( f(x - 3) \)? How does this align with your understanding of function transformations?

turn_history.text: Um, I guess I'm not really sure now that you're asking me like that... But I don't actually know why that would be the case, or like, why the number inside the brackets would affect the vertical direction at all - shouldn't that be something outside the brackets?
